# PR #3704: Patch: follow-up to #3682 from the after-merge spot-check

Closes #3699

Repaired the #3499 worker-bloat guard in [first-load.test.ts](apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts) so it fails again when a built worker bundles the patch history. The worker test (renamed to name both files) now flags any built script containing either `holds an entry with no version` (`patch-meta.ts`'s disk reader) or `holds a patch with no version string` (`patch-meta.browser.ts`, which statically imports the 650 KB history), and its comment names both files and both markers. Nothing about #3682 is reverted; only the test file changed.

How I tested it (commands I ran and what they printed):

- `pnpm --dir apps/web build` — succeeded (vite built in ~13.7s after the wasm prebuild).
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/first-load.test.ts` — 4 passed, including the renamed worker test, actually run against `dist/` (not skipped).
- Negative direction: temporarily dropped `patchMeta()` from the worker `plugins` in `vite.config.ts` (scratch edit, never committed), rebuilt vite-only, and the worker test failed, flagging `practice.worker-*.js` and `raster.worker-*.js`. A grep of those chunks showed the matched probe is exactly `holds a patch with no version string` with the old probe absent — i.e. without this fix the test would have stayed green, and with it the #3682 regression mode is caught. Then I restored `vite.config.ts` from backup, rebuilt, and the suite is green again.
- `eslint src/net/first-load.test.ts` — clean. `git status` shows only the one test file modified.

Decisions the issue did not settle: none of substance — I followed the plan's title, comment, and filter pattern exactly, including keeping the surrounding lines and the other two `it` blocks untouched (I rejected `holds no patches` as a probe since it occurs in both files, as the plan notes). One thing a reviewer should look at twice: the negative check also flagged `raster.worker`, not just the practice worker — both inlined the browser file without the plugin, which is consistent with the worker-plugin mechanism but worth knowing the guard covers all workers.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 381s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 2s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 4s |

</details>

# #3699: Patch: follow-up to #3682 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #3682 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #3682 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42973450742)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`3a3de664a2af`). `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #3682 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts:91`: Since #3682, the #3499 test 'no built script, a worker's included, holds patch-meta.ts's disk reader' can no longer fail: a Vite bundle without `patchMeta()` now resolves `#jackioh-patch-meta` to `patch-meta.browser.ts`, which statically imports the whole 650 KB `patches.json`, and the test's probe string is not in that file, so the bloat it guards against now ships with every test green.
  Evidence: The test treats a bundle as a regression only if it contains the literal "holds an entry with no version" (first-load.test.ts:97). Before #3682, a bundle without the plugin (the practice worker's own plugin list, vite.config.ts:57) fell through to `patch-meta.ts`, whose code carries that string, so the test caught it. After #3682, apps/web/package.json maps the `browser` condition to `patch-meta.browser.ts`. Vite's client and worker resolution applies the `browser` condition, so such a bundle now gets the browser file instead. Its error strings are "is not a list of patches", "holds a patch with no version string" and "holds no patches". The PR says it chose them on purpose to keep the probe 'specific to patch-meta.ts'. Its own new comment in vite.config.ts:56 says that without `patchMeta()` the worker would bundle the 650 KB history. The other #3499 guards miss this: the probe-text and gzip tests read only the entry chunk and its preloads (`entryAndPreloads()`), which leaves out worker chunks, and the 'no static import of patches.json' test scans only `src/`, while the browser file sits at the package root. Fix: make the worker test also flag any built script holding a marker that only the browser file carries, such as its "holds a patch with no version string" error, and update the test's comment to name both files.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
